report.title: OWNER BRIEFING
report.preparedFor: Prepared for D.C. Clark Custom Homes & Contracting

goals.d: Grow revenue past $3M while protecting gross margin on every build and remodel.
Segment material, labor, and overhead on every project so bids are accurate and margin is protected.
Match crews and materials to the build schedule, and keep the lead pipeline full and followed up.

highlight: Revenue reached $312K in June, up 7.6% from May and 11.4% year-over-year, the strongest month of 2026. Gross margin expanded to 24.8% as tighter cost segmentation and lower material waste took hold. Cost per square foot fell again, reflecting sharper bidding and better crew and material planning. With a full pipeline heading into Q3, the focus now is protecting margin as build volume grows.

takeaways.d: Revenue grew 7.6% in June to $312K, the best month of the year, as two custom builds and a kitchen remodel hit billing milestones.
Gross margin climbed to 24.8%, up 1.9 pts from May. Segmenting material, labor, and overhead on each project is showing exactly where margin is won or lost.
Material waste fell to 4.1% of spend, down from 6.8% in January. Better takeoffs and crew planning mean fewer reorders and less scrap on site.

comparisons.title: REVENUE (MONTHLY)
comparisons.note: June was the highest revenue month of 2026 year-to-date.

comparisons.title: COST PER SQUARE FOOT
comparisons.note: Down $16/sq ft since January. Tighter bids and less waste.

comparisons.title: GROSS MARGIN %
comparisons.note: Up 5.4 pts since January as cost segmentation took hold.

insights.d: Breaking every project into material, labor, and overhead shows where margin actually comes from. Materials are running ~44% of revenue and labor ~26%. Watch both by project type.
Weekly planning is cutting downtime and rush orders. Right-sized crews and staged deliveries keep builds moving and waste low.
Trimming waste from 6.8% to 4.1% added margin without raising a single price. Protect this. Tight takeoffs and material staging are the levers.

insights.t: Your Lead Follow-Up Is Leaking Revenue
insights.d: Custom-home leads go cold without fast, consistent follow-up. Automating first response and nurture on every inquiry turns more estimates into signed contracts.

bullets: Break every estimate into material, labor, overhead, and a waste allowance.
Compare bid vs. actual on recent jobs to sharpen the next one.
actions.step: Pull your last 3 completed projects and calculate true material, labor, and overhead cost per project this week.

actions.t: Plan Crews & Materials to the Schedule
bullets: Match crew size to each phase; stage material deliveries to the build calendar.
Fewer rush orders and less on-site waste.
actions.step: Hold a Friday planning huddle to lock crews and material drops for the next two weeks.

bullets: Put every new inquiry into an automatic follow-up sequence: text, email, and a callback reminder.
Never let an estimate request sit more than an hour.
actions.step: Set up an auto-response plus a 5-touch follow-up for new leads so no contact slips through the cracks.

closing: You're building the right way: growing revenue, protecting margin, and cutting waste. Keep segmenting your costs, planning crews and materials to the schedule, and following up fast on every lead. Do that, and the profit follows.

meta.blurb: Margin and cost per square foot, tracked against a build schedule that moves.
